newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil eases on crude slump.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil eases on crude slump.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were down slightly at midday on Friday relative to the big falls to overnight crude values as the local physical market is expected to be supported should it be offered lower, traders said.
"The gas oil is down slightly compared to crude because there are a lot of people who will support the physical market if it is offered down aggressively," a trader said.
July swaps were indicated at $21.90/$22.00 per barrel, down 25 cents from Wednesday while August was quoted 30 cents lower at $22.50/$22.60, brokers said.
July traded twice this morning at $21.90 with August done at $22.60 and $22.55, they said.
Traders said said gas oil's modest fall compared to the 71-cent cut in overnight August Brent crude to close at $18.21 a barrel on the IPE was due to expectations of physical support.
Offers which were close to $21.50 per barrel were expected to entice substantial buying interest with most pegging the physical market to close at around $21.70 late in the day, traders said.
On Thursday, the lowest offer in the physical market was at $164 per tonne ($22.00 per barrel) compared to a trade on Wednesday at $163 per tonne.
Traders said improved sentiment could also be attributed to a big draw in Singapore's middle distillate stocks.
Figures showed stocks fell for the first time since end May, by 1.331 million barrels to 10.744 million in the week ended July 2.
But the 10.744-million-barrel stock level is still high compared to the normal levels of between six million and eight million barrels, other traders said.
This high level of stocks was dampening sentiment as players feared a sudden surge in offers should the much talked about buying interest from China failed to materialise.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread was steady with July regrade last quoted at $1.80/$2.00 per barrel.
Fuel oil was also down slightly with July swaps quoted at $98.50/$99.25 per tonne, compared to Thursday's $99.00/$99.50, brokers said.
